suppressed.title: Load pets lazily instead of eager collection fetch
suppressed.summary: The eager `pets` association forces owner loads to bring back the entire pet collection even when the caller only needs owner fields.

suggestion.rationale: This avoids loading the child rows unless the collection is actually accessed, so owner-only reads do less work and fetch fewer columns/rows.
suggestion.equivalenceArgument: This changes when pet rows are loaded, so it is not equivalent; the returned owner object still exposes the same pets collection, but lazy loading defers that data and can change behavior if the persistence context is closed.
assumptions: Callers that access `getPets()` do so within an open persistence context or otherwise fetch pets explicitly.
suggestion.expectedImpact: Owner reads that do not touch pets avoid the additional collection fetch; accesses that do touch pets still work but are deferred.

suppressed.title: Make visit loading lazy
suppressed.summary: The eager `visits` association forces every loaded pet to hydrate its visit collection even when the caller does not need it.

suggestion.rationale: Lazy loading defers reading visits until code actually touches the collection, so pet loads do not automatically join or fetch child rows.
suggestion.equivalenceArgument: This is not equivalent: it changes when the visit rows are loaded and can change observable SQL timing and lazy-initialization behavior, even though the mapped rows and ordering are unchanged when the collection is accessed.
assumptions: Callers that need visits will access the collection inside an open persistence context or will be updated to fetch them explicitly.
suggestion.expectedImpact: Avoids loading visit rows for pet reads that never inspect the collection; when visits are needed, the database work is deferred to the actual access site.
suggestion.requiredMigration: ALTER TABLE visits ADD CONSTRAINT fk_visits_pets FOREIGN KEY (pet_id) REFERENCES pets (id);

evidence.relevance: Shows the child table and its foreign-key/indexed relationship that the eager collection reads from.

evidence.quote:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS visits (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  pet_id INT(4) UNSIGNED,
  visit_date DATE,
  description VARCHAR(255),
  FOREIGN KEY (pet_id) REFERENCES pets(id)
) engine=InnoDB;
evidence.relevance: Confirms the same parent-child table relationship in the MySQL schema.

suppressed.title: Load specialties lazily and fetch them only when needed
suppressed.summary: The eager many-to-many on `Vet.specialties` forces specialty rows to be loaded whenever a vet is materialized, even if the caller never reads them.

suggestion.rationale: This defers loading the join table and specialty rows until the association is actually accessed, so plain vet reads do less database work.
suggestion.equivalenceArgument: This is not equivalent: it changes when related rows are loaded and can change lazy-loading exceptions or query timing, although it preserves the same vet columns and association contents when accessed.
assumptions: Callers that need specialties access them inside an open persistence context or fetch them explicitly.
The application does not rely on eager initialization side effects during vet loading.
suggestion.expectedImpact: Avoids loading specialty associations for vet reads that do not use them; when specialties are needed, they are fetched only on demand.

evidence.quote:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vet_specialties (
  vet_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  specialty_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (vet_id) REFERENCES vets(id),
  FOREIGN KEY (specialty_id) REFERENCES specialties(id),
  UNIQUE (vet_id,specialty_id)
) engine=InnoDB;
evidence.relevance: Shows the association is materialized through a separate join table, so eager loading pulls extra rows.
Confirms the same join-table relationship exists in the H2 schema.
